subject: Geopolitics
title: India-Pakistan Water Tensions
description: A micro-lesson that makes India-Pakistan Water Tensions usable.

hook.text: The Indus Waters Treaty has survived three wars. But India threatened to revisit it after a 2019 terror attack.

buildup.text: Signed in 1960, the treaty splits six rivers between India and Pakistan. It's one of the Cold War's quiet successes.

discovery.text: Pakistan depends on the Indus for 90% of its agriculture. If India diverts water upstream, crops die.

twist.text: Climate change is melting Himalayan glaciers that feed both rivers. Less ice means less water for everyone.

climax.text: Water could become the trigger that nuclear deterrence can't contain. Thirsty nations take desperate risks.

punchline.text: The most dangerous weapon may flow from a glacier.

quiz.question: What percentage of Pakistan's agriculture depends on the Indus river system?
